subject: Re: PayGrid model fit evaluation \u0014 next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@paygrid.com>, Maya Lopez <maya@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-21T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: PayGrid model fit evaluation  recap + recommended next steps

Hi Samir / Maya 

Great to speak earlier today, thanks for the context on PayGrid's fraud-screening flow and the latency/precision targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap of needs:
- Primary goal: match or beat your current proprietary baseline on transaction-level precision/recall for fraud flags while keeping p99 latency under 220ms for single-request scoring.
- Data: you can provide a 5k-10k representative validation set (anonymized) + a small set of human-labeled edge cases we should prioritize.
- Non-functional: SRE needs audit logs + tokenization determinism for reproducibility, Procurement asked for a sample SOW and draft pricing.

Model recommendations for the eval (initial):
- Open candidates (cost-friendly): Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8/q4), Llama-3-13B (q4o)  good for high throughput and lower cost.
- Higher-capacity open option: Llama-3-70B (quantized), if you need better long-tail reasoning.
- Reference baseline: your current in-house model + our Redwood-verified production profile on GPT-4-class (for an apples-to-apples latency/quality comparison).

Evaluation plan & acceptance thresholds (proposal):
- Automated metrics: target >=95% of baseline on task-level accuracy/F1 (we'll use the metric you prefer  we noted precision-focused).
- Human QA: <5% user-visible regressions on a 200-case human sample (we'll run a blind A/B).
- Performance: p50 latency within 20% of baseline, p99 <=220ms.

Attachments I'm sharing: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (prompts + rubric), and a small benchmark template we use to collect metrics.

Next steps:
1) You share the anonymized validation set + edge-case list (upload to the Drive folder we agreed on).
2) We run the first pass evaluations against Mistral-7B and Llama-3-13B and return a short parity report within 5 business days.
3) If parity looks promising we run the 2-week POC on a dedicated test capacity with one of the higher-capacity variants.

Doable from your side? Happy to adjust thresholds if you want a stricter SLA for p99.

Thanks 
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0119

--
Attachment: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set, 220KB stub)

From: Samir Khatri <samir@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Lopez <maya@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit evaluation  recap + recommended next steps

Thanks Lauren  very helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we hand over the validation set:

1) For the automated metric parity, when you say 95% of baseline on F1, do you mean relative (95% of our absolute F1) or within 5 percentage points? For some of our filters the baseline F1 is already high (0.92), so a relative metric could be tricky.
2) Can you confirm what you consider a user-visible regression? For us that's "a false negative that changes fraud disposition"  would that be the same definition on your end?
3) Security question: our Legal wants to ensure the eval runs in a sandboxed environment with no persistent logs for raw transactions. Will Redwood run locally in our VPC for the POC, or do you need hashed records to run on hosted infra?

Also copying procurement (procurement@paygrid.com)  they asked for an initial POC SOW and an estimated price for a 2-week dedicated test (including a 70B quantized option).

If you can address the three bullets above, we'll be ready to package the anonymized dataset and the 200-case human QA panel.

Cheers,
Samir
Head of ML Engineering | PayGrid

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@paygrid.com>, procurement@paygrid.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit evaluation  recap + recommended next steps

Samir  quick answers inline, and attaching the benchmark CSV for the metrics we plan to report.

1) Parity metric type: we typically use absolute thresholds (percentage points) to avoid ambiguity  so "within 5 percentage points of your baseline F1" (e.g., baseline 0.92 -> target >=0.87). Happy to tighten to 2pp if you prefer.
2) User-visible regression definition: we will use your suggested definition: a false negative that changes fraud disposition. We'll instrument the blind A/B test to capture disposition changes and surface cases.
3) Security/infra: for the POC we can run in your VPC (Redwood Private) or in an isolated hosted sandbox with no persistent raw logs  whichever you prefer. VPC is straightforward for the 2-week test and satisfies Legal; we will provide a short SOW that calls this out.

I've attached open-vs-prop-benchmarks.csv (template & initial comparison) and re-attached paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json. Also linking the evaluation rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-paygrid-evals

Next logistical steps:
- Procurement: we'll send a 2-week POC SOW + pricing estimate by EOD tomorrow.
- Technical: once we have the validation set we'll start the 5-business-day run and deliver the parity report.

Let me know if you want the 2pp parity threshold instead of 5pp  happy to update.

Best,
Lauren

--
Attachments: open-vs-prop-benchmarks.csv (5KB stub), paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (220KB stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit evaluation  recap + proposed MAP

Samir / Lauren  jumping in with a concrete Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that we can attach to the SOW / HubSpot deal so procurement has clarity. This mirrors what Lauren outlined but adds milestones and owners.

MAP (high level):
Week 0 (today)  Agreement on thresholds & security model (Procurement + Legal sign-off). Owner: PayGrid
Week 1  Dataset handoff (PayGrid) + Redwood starts 5-business-day automated runs on two open candidates (Mistral-7B, Llama-3-13B). Owner: PayGrid / Redwood
Week 2  Deliver parity report (metrics + blind A/B human QA); decide on candidate for 2-week POC. Owner: Redwood
Week 3-4  2-week POC on dedicated capacity (option for Llama-3-70B quantized if needed). Deliverables: integration guide, audit logs, performance dashboard. Owner: Redwood
Post-POC  Pricing/ordering conversation; option to move to Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on throughput & security needs. Owner: Sales + Solutions

Parity acceptance criteria (proposal to include in SOW):
- Automated: >= baseline - 5 percentage points on your chosen metric(s) (or >= baseline - 2pp if PayGrid wants more conservative bar).
- Human QA: <5% user-visible regressions on 200-case panel.
- Performance: p99 <=220ms on the chosen test traffic profile OR within 20% of your current baseline.

Prep items we need from PayGrid:
- Anonymized validation dataset (S3/Drive link)
- 200-case human QA panel (names or redacted IDs + labels)
- Legal/procurement contact for SOW approval

I'll draft the MAP + a short SOW and put it in the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/PG-2027-0421  assigning a draft to Procurement for signature.

If that looks good we'll attach the MAP to the SOW and Lauren will send the pricing estimate.

Thanks 
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: redwood-parity-thresholds.pdf (proposal, 130KB stub)
